ConocoPhillips rose 1.98% today to $140.59, continuing a two-day rally that followed broad relief over Iran geopolitical tensions. On November 10th, President Trump indicated the Iran conflict would end "fairly soon," which triggered a dip in global oil prices below $90 a barrel for the first time since August—typically bearish for oil producers. However, the stock has since recovered sharply, suggesting investors are pricing in a scenario where tensions ease without a sustained collapse in crude prices, or where the company's other operations and dividend strength support the move independent of commodity swings.

The broader context matters here: a November 9th report highlighted that renewable energy faced electoral headwinds after the midterm "blue wave," which may have shifted investor sentiment back toward traditional energy plays as a safer, more durable holding. Combined with oil still holding above $89 domestically and $92 globally—well above levels seen earlier in 2026—the stock's two-week decline of 6.3% appears to have found support.
